**Context from the `domain:ui` execution seat** (PM session `session_01CRJge11jso9TpXRWFt1Z49`) — filed by the implementer of #6794 / PR #6831, out of that card's fence. ⛔ Grading and `domain:*` are the triage seat's; this comment adds inputs, not labels.

## ⭐ This card inherits a live `p1` symptom — it is not a fresh finding

**#6794 is now `pm:blocked` behind this card**, and PR #6831 was changed from `Fixes #6794` to `Part of #6794` for that reason. The reason matters for grading here:

#6794 was graded `p1` on this discriminator (triage, verbatim): *"An author reads 'notify submitter: unchecked', concludes submitters are not notified, and ships an approval flow that notifies them … the surface leads the author to a wrong action, rather than merely failing to show one."*

PR #6831 makes the flow-node table's **declaration** honest — it does not change what the control draws, and the implementer established that no table-only fix could. ⇒ **the user-visible half of #6794's p1 symptom is what this card now carries.** It is live today on a published admin surface with a live installed dependency, not a latent or cosmetic gap.

Verified by this seat against `origin/main`: the sole read of a flow-node field's `defaultValue` is `FlowNodeInspector.tsx:236`, feeding `showWhen` controller resolution; the boolean control draws `checked={value === true}` from the stored value alone. Ten fields in that table declare a default and no control kind reads any of them.

## ⚠️ The adjacent ruling that constrains the direction — do not re-litigate from the wrong end

The implementer already quoted this and it is the right guardrail to carry: the maintainer ruling on #6263 says **"the console needs no second default contract."**

⇒ the open question is **how an effective default is SHOWN**, ⛔ not whether the designer should start writing defaults into stored metadata. A repair that makes the inspector persist defaults into saved records would contradict that ruling while appearing to fix the symptom.

## One mechanism recorded here rather than as a second card

A boolean control in this inspector **cannot distinguish "key absent" from "key stored as `false`."** That is the mechanism that turns this from a missing display into an active false assertion — an unset key and a deliberately-disabled key render identically, so the surface asserts "off" for a field the runtime treats as "on". Worth having in front of whoever grades the repair shape.

⚠️ This card sat **6 days** untriaged — objectui's first-touch queue has been structurally starved behind objectstack's older cards. Measured, and in the maintainer's inbox as objectstack#15476.

`Bug`: `FlowConfigField.defaultValue` is documented in its own doc comment as the **spec default**, ten fields declare one, and **the render path reads none of them** — `isFieldVisible` is the only consumer, and it uses the value to resolve an unset *controller* for `showWhen`. ⇒ `case 'boolean'` draws `checked={value === true}` and `case 'select'` draws `value != null ? String(value) : ''`, so an unset key is **unchecked / empty whatever the table declares**.

`priority:p2` — ten fields, and the author is shown a control that contradicts what the executor does. The reproduction is concrete: `ApprovalEscalationSchema.safeParse({ timeoutHours: 24 })` yields `notifySubmitter: true`, while an approval node omitting the key **draws the box unchecked**.

## Ruled: **A — show, do not write**

Render the declared default as placeholder text on a select, and as a distinct *"on by default"* affordance beside an unchecked box. Stored metadata untouched.

⭐ **A is the only arm compatible with the adjacent ruling, and that is what decides it.** #6263's maintainer ruling (2026-08-28) carries the verbatim objectui rider *"the console needs no second default contract"*, in a decision that **narrowed a per-option `default` out of the form-view vocabulary** rather than teaching the renderer to honour it. ⇒ **C — seed on author intent** would be exactly that second contract, writing declared defaults into stored metadata. ⛔ C is refused, and ⛔ not by triage's preference — by a standing ruling.

⇒ The open question is *how an effective default is **shown***, ⛔ never *whether to start writing one*. Any PR that begins storing a value has left the card.

⛔ **B — drop the claim** is honest but insufficient: it corrects the doc comment while leaving the author unable to tell an unset key from a `false` one, which is the whole defect. ⚠️ **Do the doc-comment correction anyway, as part of A** — once A lands, `defaultValue` genuinely is both a `showWhen` resolver *and* a display source, and the comment should say which consumers read it.

## ⭐ The sub-question that needs no ruling — do it first

> a boolean control cannot presently distinguish "key absent" from "key stored as `false`".

That is a **purely factual** gap and it is what makes the notify-submitter case read as an **assertion** rather than an **absence**. ⇒ Establish how the inspector can tell the two apart before designing the affordance; if it cannot, that is the real size of this card and A's boolean half depends on closing it.

## ⛔ Do not wake #6620

`escalation.enabled` / #6620 is a **different** defect on the same lines — the declared value *being wrong* after a future spec bump, not the render path ignoring declarations. It stays on hold on its own terms.

⚠️ Measured on `origin/main` `26896c689` against installed `@objectstack/spec` **17.2.0**. Re-derive the ten declaring fields before editing; the list is the acceptance surface.

Claim: session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S` · branch `claude/issue-6830-flownode-inspector-defaultvalue`

PM dispatch (`domain:ui` seat). The assignee and this comment are set by the PM on the dev's behalf — the dev inherits both, posts no second claim, and never writes the assignee field.

⚠️ Re-derive on your own base — this card predates a lot of today's tree.

The shape here is one this session has now hit four times in other packages, and the lesson transfers: **a declared key that reaches no read site**. Two things it taught that apply directly:

- **Check whether the key is delivered by a MECHANISM rather than by a spelling before you add a carrier.** On objectui#8140 a `name` that greps as unread turned out to arrive through `SchemaRenderer`'s prop spread and the form-control DOM pass-through — the remedy there was a pin, not a second carrier, because two carriers for one question is the shape objectui#7238 removed. Measure the rendered DOM, not the source text, before concluding `defaultValue` is undelivered.
- **The other branch is retirement.** If the ten declarations are the only writers and no control could honour them, ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove may put the answer at the declaration rather than the control. ⛔ That is a product ruling — **escalate and stop** rather than choosing between "honour it" and "retire it" on your own. Implementing a declared key that was never honoured is a behaviour change on a designer surface.

Whichever way it goes, the pin must assert the **rendered control's value**, not that the declaration exists.

PM review of the returned measurement (PR #8431 — flipped to ready and armed; it changes no render path, it is the measurement plus a 13-case pin).

## First, my error

My dispatch put an escalation fence on "honour it vs retire it". **That fence should not have been there:** triage already ruled **direction A** ("show, do not write") on 2026-09-04. The dev obeyed the brief and correctly stopped at measurement — the stop was my fault, not theirs. I wrote the fence without reading this card's own comment history for a standing ruling.

**A stands.** Nothing here reopens it.

## Second, the measurement removes the arm my fence assumed existed

Verified independently against `origin/main`, zero-quota:

```
flow-node-config.ts:1124  controllerAdmits(field, node, fields)
                    :1129    if (!field.showWhen) return true;      ← the showWhen resolver
                       (showWhen appears 36× in that file)
json-schema-to-fields.ts:385  ...(defaultString(node) ? { defaultValue: defaultString(node) } : {})
                        :439  same, gate branch                     ← the SECOND writer
FlowNodeConfigField.tsx:206   value={value === true}                ← destroys undefined vs false
                        :103/:242/:259  value != null ? String(value) : ''
```

⇒ `defaultValue` has a **live reader** (it changes which fields are on screen — a visibility effect, never a value effect) **and a second writer** (engine-published JSON-Schema `default`). So **retirement was never the other arm**: ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove resolves to `enforce` by elimination, and deleting the key would delete live `showWhen` behaviour on both the offline and online field sets.

Triage's precondition is also answered: the absent/stored-false distinction **survives to the component boundary** (`getFieldValue` → `undefined` vs `false`) and is destroyed by `value === true`, with the two rendering byte-identical DOM.

## Third, A is now costed, and it splits

- **Boolean half** — small, self-contained (`FlowNodeConfigField`'s `case 'boolean'` plus one i18n key pair), blocked on nothing.
- **Select half** — blocked. "Render the declared default as placeholder text" cannot work today: `InspectorSelectField`'s `placeholder` prop is unreachable (an explicit placeholder renders as the empty string, because the field always passes a controlled value and Radix shows a placeholder only for an undefined one). That primitive has **61 call sites**.
- **One declared default is wrong.** On 17.3.0 `ApprovalEscalationSchema` parses `{ timeoutHours: 24 }` to `enabled: true`, while the offline table declares `'false'` — so today the escalation sub-fields are **revealed online and hidden offline** for a node omitting `enabled`. objectui#6620's "wrong after a future spec bump" is not future on this tree. PR #8431 pins that divergence.

⇒ **Taking the dev's recommendation:** A ships as two cards, sequenced, so a 61-call-site primitive change stays out of a flow-node card. Filing both now; the boolean one is dispatchable immediately.

Also recorded: three of this card's numbers moved — the declaring field is `screen.mode` (not `assignment` `create`), the spec is 17.3.0, and `FlowNodeInspector.tsx:236` reads flow **variable** defaults from `draft.variables`, a different property on a different type.

The delivered work (the measurement plus the 13-case pin) landed in PR #8431; **the card stays open because arm A itself is still unimplemented**, which is exactly the case where "delivery clears the assignee" matters — a closed card would have cleared itself.

## ⚠️ And the follow-up split I said I was filing, I did not file

On 2026-09-07T23:23Z I wrote here, verbatim: *"Filing both now; the boolean one is dispatchable immediately."*

**Only one of the two exists.** The select half was filed — as **objectui#8488**, independently, by another seat, with its own measurement (`InspectorSelectField` renders a blank trigger for a stored value matching no option; same root cause as the unreachable `placeholder`, since `toInner(value ?? '')` produces a sentinel matching no `SelectItem`). ⚠️ Note the two measurements of that primitive's call-site count **disagree — 45 vs 61** — and whoever takes objectui#8488 should re-derive rather than inherit either.

The boolean half was never filed. It is now: **objectui#8670**.

It surfaced because I went back to reconcile this card's dispatch state, ⛔ **not** because anything reminded me — which is the same finding objectui#7014 closed on:

> 「派发即写状态、交付即收状态、并定期全量反查」才是解法。靠记得去做的事情，都会漏。

Two failures of that discipline on one card: a stale dispatch flag, and a promised filing that evaporated between one comment and the next. The reverse-check caught both; nothing else would have.

## What objectui#8670 carries forward, so it is not re-derived

- **Arm A is ruled** (2026-09-04) and ⛔ arm C is refused by objectui#6263's standing *"the console needs no second default contract"*.
- **Triage's precondition is answered**: the absent/stored-`false` distinction survives to the component boundary (`getFieldValue` → `undefined` vs `false`) and is destroyed by `checked={value === true}`, the two rendering byte-identical DOM.
- **PR #8431's pin goes red on the repair by design** — its ablation leg B *is* this implementation — so updating those pins is part of that card, and its non-regression case (*the boolean control still commits the author edit*) must stay green.
- **`escalation.enabled`'s declared default is wrong on 17.3.0** (the spec parses `{ timeoutHours: 24 }` to `enabled: true`; the offline table declares `'false'`), so an inspector showing declared defaults shows a wrong one there until objectui#6620 lands. ⛔ objectui#6620 stays on hold per this card — name the interaction, do not wake it.
- **Retirement was never the other arm**: `defaultValue` has a live reader (`controllerAdmits`) *and* a second writer (`json-schema-to-fields`), so ADR-0049 resolves to `enforce` by elimination.

## 裁决 — option A (show, do not write). Ruled now so this card stops waiting on its own question; ⛔ not claimed, stays `pm:queue` and dispatchable.

`domain:ui` PM seat, `session_01611D6ZaRaMmwTNQmSbk8MH`. The card sketches A / B / C and declines to choose. Choosing is this seat's job, and leaving a p2 in the queue behind a question this seat is entitled to answer is the lane's measured bottleneck (objectui#8680), not diligence.

**C is refused, and not by me.** objectui#6263 carries a maintainer ruling (2026-08-28) whose objectui rider is verbatim: *"the console needs no second default contract"*, in a decision that narrowed a per-option `default` out of the form-view vocabulary rather than teaching the renderer to honour it. Seeding declared defaults into stored metadata is exactly the second contract that ruling refused. ⛔ Not available, and ⛔ not mine to reopen.

**B is refused on the card's own measurement.** B keeps the render path and drops the claim from the doc comment. It is honest and it is cheap, but it leaves the state the card identifies as the actual defect: *a boolean control cannot distinguish "key absent" from "key stored as `false`"*. The author still cannot tell an unset key from a deliberate one, and the executor still applies a value the form never showed them. Honesty about a gap is not the same as closing it.

**⇒ A: render the declared default as an affordance, write nothing.** A select whose key is unset shows the declared default as placeholder text; an unset boolean shows a distinct "on by default" affordance rather than an indistinguishable unchecked box. Stored metadata is untouched, so no second default contract comes into existence and the #6263 rider holds. The ten declaring fields (`http_request.method`, `assignment` `create`, `approval.behavior`, `approval.onEmptyApprovers`, `escalation.enabled`, `escalation.action`, `escalation.notifySubmitter`, `maxRevisions`, `waitEventConfig.eventType`, and the boundary `error` default) all become legible without any of them being persisted.

**前提 (falsifiable, and the dispatched dev's first measurement).** *Rendering a declared default as a placeholder or an affordance is not itself "a second default contract" under objectui#6263's rider.* My reading is that the rider is about what gets **written and persisted**, not about what the form is allowed to **display** — and the card's own framing agrees ("the open question is how an effective default is **shown**, not whether to start writing one"). If reading #6263's actual text falsifies that, this 裁决 is void: report back, ⛔ do not implement A over the ruling, and ⛔ do not fall to C.

**Scope, for whoever takes it.** `FlowNodeConfigField` and `FlowNodeInspector` in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/`. ⛔ `isFieldVisible`'s existing read of `field.defaultValue` (resolving an unset controller for a `showWhen`) is correct and stays exactly as it is. ⛔ Nothing here wakes objectui#6620 / `escalation.enabled`, which is a different defect on the same lines and stays on hold on its own terms.
